label: Arkenda
description: Arkenda 0.2.0: a local-first, private Markdown notes app for Linux, Windows, Android and the web.

children.label: Getting started
children.description: Install Arkenda 0.2.0 on Linux, Windows, Android or the web, and open your first vault.

children.label: Folder vaults (desktop)
children.description: On the desktop app, a vault can be a folder on your disk. The folder is the source of truth: your notes are plain .md files you can open, edit, move, sync or version with any other tool, and Arkenda follows those…

children.label: Guides
children.description: How to use Arkenda 0.2.0: vaults, layout, shortcuts, media, sync and more.

children.label: The desktop layout
children.description: On a window wider than 1023 px (the desktop app, and the web app on a large screen; a tablet shares most of it), Arkenda shows four panes side by side: the sidebar on the left, the note list, the note with its tabs…

children.label: Keyboard shortcuts
children.description: Arkenda's default keys follow the conventions shared by Google Docs, Word, Confluence, Notion, Obsidian and VS Code. Almost every key below can be changed or removed in Settings ▸ Keyboard, which also prints a cheat…

children.label: Media
children.description: Pictures, audio, video and other files live in your vault next to your notes. Everything here works on the device: nothing is sent to a service to be read, converted or recognised.

children.label: Sync between your devices
children.description: Arkenda syncs a vault between the devices you paired, with no account and no server of ours in the middle. Turn it on in Settings ▸ Sync & devices ▸ Overview (its guided setup names this device, turns sync on and…

children.label: The activity island

children.label: Overview
children.description: A plugin is an ES module that runs in a sandbox and talks to Arkenda only through ctx. It can read and change notes, add commands, panels, widgets, editor items, Markdown blocks, themes and settings, and fetch…

children.label: Getting started
children.description: Build a "Reading time" plugin: a sidebar panel that shows how long the open note takes to read.

children.label: Plugin API
children.description: Build an extension with any tooling, language or layout you like. To be supported it must meet one contract: the manifest, the package, the entry point, the permission and sandbox rules, and the API version. bun…

children.label: Manifest reference
children.description: arkenda-plugin.json describes an extension before any of its code runs: who made it, what it is, what it asks for and what it adds. The app's validator (parsePluginManifestV2) is the authority; manifest.schema.json…

children.label: The package and release
children.description: A package is a .zip (or, in developer mode, a folder) holding the manifest, one bundle and a few assets. Arkenda reads it without running it, checks every file, and installs it only when it passes.

children.label: Permissions and privacy
children.description: Ask only for what you use: users see every permission before they install, and grant each one when they turn the plugin on. Every call is checked against the grant at the moment it is made.

children.label: The sandbox
children.description: Each enabled third-party plugin runs isolated from the app, talks to it only through checked messages, and is stopped when it breaks a limit. Built-in plugins run in-process and are not sandboxed.

children.label: API reference
children.description: Generated from @arkenda/kit/plugin-api (to be published as @arkenda/plugin-api) and its JSDoc. API version 1.0: ctx.apiVersion is 1, ctx.apiMinor is 0.

children.label: Surfaces
children.description: Where a plugin can show, and when to use each place. Declare every item in contributes first: the app shows titles from there before any code runs, and refuses an undeclared id (not-declared).

children.label: Settings
children.description: A plugin declares its settings as data; Arkenda renders them on the plugin's page (the Options gear on its card, shown while the plugin is on). A plugin never renders its own settings HTML.

children.label: UX guidelines
children.description: A plugin should feel like part of Arkenda. For sandboxed plugins most of this is automatic, because the app renders their views, settings and menus with its own components; what is left is the words, the structure…

children.label: Testing a plugin
children.description: Check the contract with the app's own tools, test your logic against a fake ctx, then try the real thing in developer mode.

children.label: Security checklist
children.description: Use it before you ship a plugin, and when you review someone else's. The sandbox limits the damage a plugin can do; this list keeps it from asking for more than it needs.

children.label: Versioning and compatibility
children.description: Three numbers decide whether a plugin runs: its own version, the apiVersion it was built for and the minAppVersion it needs.

children.label: Worked examples
